The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 13:20 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members, the proceedings of today's National Assembly meeting
(13:20 hrs)
commence. Honourable Members, time has been requested to speak during the Zero Hour. I have set a maximum time limit of 3 minutes for speaking during the Zero Hour. I will now provide time to the Honourable Members sequentially. First, Honourable Member Rajenralaxmi Gaire.
Honourable Mr. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepali Communist Party):-
Right Honourable
(13:21 hrs)
Chairperson, following the great disaster on Bhadra 10, continuous rainfall since Ashoj 8 has caused great disasters across the country. Among these, Palpa district has received the most rainfall and suffered the most damage. Palpa district has 10 local levels: two municipalities and eight rural municipalities. Today, there are no roads connecting one local level to another in all ten local levels. Everything is blocked by landslides.
Similarly, in that area, in Ridi Khola Rural Municipality, Krishna Kumari Saru, aged 49, died when a landslide swept away her house. Similarly, in Mathagadhi Rural Municipality Ward No. 2, Rapse, Sher Bahadur Chidi, aged 75, also died, his house was swept away, and in Ward No. 3, Kaseni of Mathagadhi, Lil Bahadur Gharti and his 17 and 15-year-old children were also swept away by the landslide, and their houses were buried. This incident occurred on the morning of the 11th. Their livestock also perished, carried away by the landslide. I offer my heartfelt condolences to those who lost their lives in this great disaster and express my highest respect to all the warriors who have been working day and night to provide assistance during this calamity. In Palpa district, the Kaligandaki River has had a significant impact. The Kaligandaki bridge connecting Palpa-Syangja, Chapakot and Rampur, the Keladi bridge, has been damaged. Vehicles coming to Kathmandu via the Keladi bridge also use that route, and it has also been damaged. Keladi bridge, Hugi bridge, Ramdi bridge. Similarly, the Mirmi bridge connecting Harmachaur has been washed away.
We have also heard that the ward office building in Baglung has been washed away, and Rani Mahal, known as Rani Mahal in Palpa, is precariously perched, surrounded by the Kaligandaki River. Resorts and houses in its vicinity have also been damaged. Therefore, many fields and farms in Palpa, Rampur Phant and Mardi Phant, and Argali Phant, where two crops are grown annually, have been destroyed. I draw the attention of all stakeholders to this disaster... (Time expired).
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota.
(13:24 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Samjhana Devkota (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Right Honourable
(13:24 hrs)
Chairperson, before we could recover from the pain of the Bhote Koshi flood, we are facing another disaster. Due to continuous rainfall for about four days starting today, all districts have been affected. Among them, Manang and Mustang, considered the roof of Gandaki Province, have experienced severe floods and heavy rainfall. This has affected the Marshyangdi, Kaligandaki, Trishuli, and Budhigandaki rivers. This has caused significant loss of life and property. According to the information received so far, 21 people have died, many families have been displaced, 419 families are displaced, and there has been a loss of life and property exceeding 145 people, with many houses also partially damaged. Livestock and government buildings have been damaged, and major highways, including the Mid-Hill Highway and Prithvi Highway, are also blocked. This has even affected the Narayangadh market and the Gaindakot market in Nawalpur, which have never experienced such damage; many markets are submerged.
Although the government and the National Disaster Risk Reduction Authority had issued prior warnings, the flood's impact was felt in unexpected places. This flood's impact suggests a significant disruption to the upcoming festivals and the return of people to their homes, leading to a shortage of food. This risk is also a consequence of climate change. We are suffering greatly due to climate change. Along with this, climbers attempting to ascend the mountains in the Manaslu and Mustang regions are also out of contact, and many are in a state of disarray. The government must not fail in any way at this time. Just as we suffered significant losses in the Bhote Koshi flood due to not seeking timely rescue assistance, the government must now create an environment for timely assistance and seek help from supporting organizations. The loss of life and property of the general public must be prevented.
How can we protect the people from this disaster? Currently, Tal village in Manang is completely submerged. The Marshyangdi River is blocked. Although there is a plan to break the Marshyangdi dam today to release the water, I urge the government to carefully break the dam, bring the Marshyangdi River back to its normal flow, and pay special attention to justice and the safety of all affected individuals. Gandaki Province has suffered immense damage. I urge the government to take prompt initiatives for the construction of its infrastructure, roads, and bridges, and I want the government's attention to be directed there. I demand that the government immediately open Manang, Prithvi Highway, and all other roads. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Puja Chaudhary.
(13:27 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Puja Chaudhary (Janata Samajwadi Party, Nepal):- Right Honourable
(13:27 hrs)
Chairperson, due to climate change, we have not yet recovered from the human and property losses in the recent Rasuwa flood caused by an avalanche, and again, due to continuous rainfall from Ashoj 8 to 11, damage has occurred in various parts of the country. Highways are blocked, and areas like Susma, Tharitole in Nawalparasi, Chitwan, Gandaki, Madhesh Province, and various other parts of the country are submerged. This has led to the displacement of many people and loss of life and property. Although we had drawn the government's attention to the preparedness for monsoon-related disasters through a motion in the National Assembly on 2083/4/6, we have also tried to alert the government about this matter from time to time. I want to draw the government's attention, through the Honourable Chairperson, to the swift rescue, relief, and management of those affected by this monsoon-related disaster.
If this situation continues, it could lead to serious health problems. There is also a significant risk of epidemics. Due to the inability to rescue those affected by the Rasuwa flood in time, many lives were lost, and relief supplies, including food, are rotting because they could not be distributed on time, while the victims have not received any relief. Therefore, its management must be expedited. The future of children is also being pushed into darkness; it is necessary to start their education, even if it is through temporary arrangements. Initiatives must also be taken for reconstruction and rehabilitation. The current situation has also affected people's lives due to the rising inflation. Inflation is high, but artificial shortages are also making life difficult.
Right Honourable Chairperson, this is increasing the risk of food and water shortages in the country. Although Madhesh Province is considered the granary of the country, if this situation persists, Madhesh Province could turn into a desert due to water and food shortages. Therefore, through the Honourable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention to reconstruction and rehabilitation. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members, the time for speaking during the Zero Hour
(13:30 hrs)
concludes. Honourable Members, names have been registered to speak during the Zero Hour. I will now provide time to the Honourable Members to speak. First, Honourable Member Ghanashyam Rizal.
Honourable Mr. Ghanashyam Rizal (Nepali Communist Party):- Right Honourable
(13:30 hrs)
Chairperson, the incident of former Chief Justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana being taken from his home at midnight without an arrest warrant, citing security reasons, raises serious questions about the working style of the security agencies and the rule of law. Illegally arresting and detaining him, and not allowing the National Human Rights Commission to meet him, is an act against the state's constitution and a dictatorial style. I strongly condemn this and want to ask the government: is the government trying to move towards authoritarianism? If not, what is the reason for arresting the former Chief Justice? What message is being sent to the judiciary by arresting him without cause? Has he been truly released, or is he still under house arrest? If there was a security threat from the Gen Z community, why is the government itself engaged in unnecessarily defaming and provoking the Gen Z? Regarding this, this respected house and... (Time expired).
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Rukmini Koirala.
(13:31 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Rukmini Koirala (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Right Honourable
(13:31 hrs)
Chairperson, the government claims to provide good governance, but is the suffering faced by the public in their daily lives today good governance? Is it not the government's duty to provide the basic needs of the people easily? I want to ask the government: has the government filled the potholes on the roads or not? Why hasn't it been done? When will it be done? Is this good governance? Wherever you look, there are potholes on the road. How many people have lost their lives, and has the government seen it? Is this good governance? How has it come to the point where two people commit suicide daily, is this good governance? Due to the road conditions, a journey that takes one hour takes five hours, and a healthy person has to be hospitalized upon reaching home, is this the government's good governance? Is it good governance that those who murdered three-year-old Garima Chaudhary were released on a bail of twenty thousand rupees?
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini.
(13:32 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Bishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable
(13:32 hrs)
Chairperson, democracy is a system that upholds the rule of law and respects human rights. It is never appropriate to try to run it with an authoritarian mindset. In this context, arresting former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, Cholendra Shumsher J.B.R., from his home while he was sleeping at night, without a warrant and without cause, is a mockery of good governance and the law. I want to caution the government, through the Honourable Chairperson, not to engage in such activities. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.
(13:33 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepali Communist Party):- Right Honourable
(13:33 hrs)
Chairperson, the country is in a crisis due to a lack of gas. The public is forced to eat dry food or raw food. However, despite having a large reserve of gas in the country, the government is unable to utilize it. It has been confirmed for two years that there is a large reserve of methane gas in Jaljale, Dailekh, Karnali Province. Why has that project not been operationalized yet? Who stopped it? What was the reason for stopping it, and in whose interest is it being stopped? The government's attention has not been drawn to this. Let the Nepalis use Nepal's gas. Let the government pay attention and expedite the production of gas from Jaljale as soon as possible. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari.
(1:34 PM)
Mr. Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepali Communist Party):- Honorable Chairperson,
(1:34 PM)
Sir, before the pain of the Bhote Koshi flood could subside, there have been huge losses of life and property across the country due to floods, landslides, and inundation. Since October 8th, continuous rainfall has caused the deaths of 21 people in Mustang, Baglung, Myagdi, Palpa, and other areas. Hundreds of houses, sheds, livestock, roads, and land have been washed away, causing significant damage in most districts including Manang, Myagdi, Baglung, Parbat, and Nawalpur. The government has dismissed the relatives of those who died in the Bhote Koshi flood, stating that there is no legal provision for death registration. Death registration should be done immediately through a special law. The displaced people have not received the promised Rs 15,000 for house rent. The government's rescue and relief efforts are ineffective. The compensation for the deceased's mourning period, compensation, temporary and permanent housing...
(Time expired.)
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Savitri Malla.
(1:36 PM)
Ms. Savitri Malla (Nepali Communist Party):- Honorable Chairperson,
(1:36 PM)
Sir, the country is in mourning. Hailstones are falling without clouds. Due to the floods in the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers on Bhadra 10th, and the continuous rainfall from Ashoj 8th to Ashoj 11th in various parts of the country, there has been a significant loss of life and property due to floods, landslides, and inundation. I offer heartfelt condolences and tribute to the citizens of the country and abroad who have died in this tragic incident, and express sympathy to the bereaved families. I seriously draw the government's attention to arrange for the rescue and relief of the injured and displaced citizens and to expedite the search for missing citizens, especially as the festivals are approaching. Due to damage to roads, bridges, and transportation routes, it will be very difficult for citizens to reach home and to transport essential goods and travel.
(Time expired.)
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Members, the order of speaking during Zero Hour ends here.
(1:37 PM)
Honorable Members, names have been received on a party basis for speaking during Special Time. Now I will provide time for the honorable members to speak. First, Honorable Member Anand Prasad Dugana, time 29 minutes. Following this, Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.
Mr. Anand Prasad Dugana (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson,
(1:37 PM)
Sir, I have brought newspapers today. All the newspapers today are about the former Chief Justice of Nepal being arrested at 1 PM at night without a warrant. What is happening in this country? It's very difficult. In the Panchayat era, when we were arrested, we knew. When King Mahendra, to save the Panchayat system, acted on Poush 1, 2017 BS, he passed a Public Security Act and we were arrested. They would come at night to arrest us. But the family members would say, 'Who are you? We don't know you. Come in civil dress.' Just like the police came in civil dress to arrest our Chief Justice today. We asked, 'Who are you? We don't know. Where is the warrant?' We haven't seen that either, so we won't let you take him. Are you going to kill him or what? So, who are you? Since we don't know, we said to take him in the morning, and we were arrested in the morning. Today, the same situation has arisen again.
When I read these newspapers and heard the news, I wondered if the Panchayat system has really started again? Then I remembered, I had said from this very rostrum that the Biratnagar Jute Mill protest was not a labor movement. It was a movement to end 104 years of autocratic rule, during which people like BP Koirala, Manmohan Adhikari, and Girija Prasad Koirala were arrested. They were not arrested for not getting food. They all fought for the rights of the people in the name of labor, raising the issues of the laborers. They were brought to Kathmandu from Dhankuta on foot. I had raised that issue from this rostrum. So, I feel that today, this government, which claims to provide good governance and empower the people, is acting in what way?
Yesterday, a message was reportedly written to Krishna Hari Pushkar by the Prime Minister! I know Krishna Hari Pushkar's house is also in Suga, and the Prime Minister's house is also in Ekadada. Both are in the same municipality, only the ward is different. And someone from his own village, his own city, might have written something as a request. But there was no basis for his arrest, yet he was arrested and kept for 12 hours, and then handed over to his wife. Today, the Chief Justice has been treated similarly. What does this show? The government is taking one step after another towards autocracy. If the political parties of this country had not fought against this autocracy for a long time, if our elders had not sacrificed themselves, had not been hanged, had not stayed in jail, I think the law that was in the mouth during the Rana regime, today also the law is in the mouth. I heard that the Prime Minister came on Saturday around 4 PM, and then it was asked through his PA at night what happened to Cholenra Shamsher, and then he was arrested saying he should be arrested. Is that true? If not, the government must answer today. Why was he arrested?
No citizen can be arrested without a crime. He was in special security. It is said that an attempt was made to provide him security. The Jengis are being defamed in his security! Yesterday, Singha Durbar was burned in the name of Jengis, yesterday the court was burned in the name of Jengis, yesterday the Parliament was burned in the name of Jengis, yesterday the President's House was burned in the name of Jengis. Today, again in the name of Jengis, you said he was insecure, the former Chief Justice, and arrested him. If there was insecurity, there were four layers of security. If there was insecurity, the army was added, and the next day his crime would have been shown and he would have been arrested. The law says so, this is what happens in a democracy. Therefore, if we are moving away from democracy, it must be said from this rostrum.
Today, the colleagues have raised the issue of flood victims. But we have suffered from floods before. The tears have not yet dried from those floods, but another one has started, from the 8th to the 11th. What is happening in this country? What happened where, who is dying, for what reason are they dying, for what reason are floods are occurring? Should this house not get information about it? Should the government not provide it here? I have been a Member of Parliament in this country's parliamentary system 5 times. Previous governments, when any incident or accident occurred, would immediately come and answer in the house. They would say, 'This is the reason, this happened here.' It was not just for the honorable members to hear, but to inform the country. Will you inform the country or not? Do you have any responsibility to the country? The Nepali people did not elect you just like that. If you are going to sit with the arrogance of having a two-thirds majority, a time may come when even the Ranas did not think they would have to leave this country. They ruled for generations, for 104 years, they did not think they would leave. Kings also did not think so for 240/242 years. When they became dictators, the Ranas also ended, the Kings also ended. Now there are neither Kings nor Ranas. Today, we Nepali people are supreme, and the representatives of the Nepali people, the powers representing the Nepali people, the Prime Minister and the Home Minister must answer, or not?
And I had said here, colleagues were speaking here, during Zero Hour. And I felt, in the past, ministers had to come and answer when issues were raised during Zero Hour. The Speaker would rule. Today, even if the Speaker rules, nothing will happen. No matter how much you speak, nothing will happen. It's like the crow keeps cawing, but the pine tree keeps drying. Therefore, what I want to say is, there is a system of governance in this country, there is real democracy, we fought and created this federal democratic republic constitution, the government must answer. I had raised the issue of Kankai before, and now there has been firing in Kankai again. I did not get an answer about Kankai either. Before this, all colleagues have said, what happens by speaking in Zero Hour? What is the point of Zero Hour? Then I was telling the colleague next to me, now I will stand in Zero Hour and cover my ears. And if the Chairperson asks why I am covering my ears, I will say the government doesn't listen, so I won't listen either, I won't speak. Is there any other way?
Therefore, what I want to say is that this government is not responsible to the Nepali people in some way. The Prime Minister is always called to the House of Representatives. The Nepali people also went and said that the dam built in India's Susta has encroached on our land. What happened when that was said? When it broke, the Indian army stopped it. Today, because of the Indian army's intervention, Susta is submerged. Who is responsible? Who will take that responsibility? Who will save the people?
Therefore, what I want to say is that the Prime Minister is responsible. The Prime Minister has done all these things. There is no need to blame anyone else here. Therefore, the Prime Minister should explain to the Nepali people. Yes, in the Rana era, when 6 sons of the Ranas came to Tundikhel for a parade, it was called hukumi law, hukumi शासन. Is that it? Are you trying to do that? If you are trying to do that, I said it yesterday too. Now the non-party system will not work. Yesterday too, we came forward to sacrifice ourselves. Yesterday too, we sacrificed to bring democracy, to bring democracy to this country. If you are trying to walk that path again today, then today the Nepali people, the youth of Nepal are ready to sacrifice, do not forget this. Therefore, I want to say that the situation created by the government in this way is not good. I don't think it will benefit Nepal. I don't believe it will provide good governance in this country and that the Nepali people will progress.
What happened in 35 years? In 35 years, you saw how many power houses were destroyed by the Bhote Koshi flood. How many bridges were destroyed? What happened? That must have been built in these 35 years. Whatever has been destroyed now, whatever has been swept away by the flood. 21 people have died in this rain from the 8th to the 11th. 747 households have been affected. But should the government come and say something here or not? Is it more or less than that, or have the newspapers exaggerated it? Should we get information from the newspapers? We should get information from the Home Minister from this rostrum. The Nepali people want to know from the rostrum what is happening in Nepal? How is the governance system running? Therefore, I want to say that the current situation is not good for the country. Wherever I go, people say to me, 'Brother, the future doesn't look good. Politics doesn't seem to be going in the right direction. How will you manage this?' You gave votes to manage it, didn't you? You voted silently for the bell symbol. You voted silently. Therefore, this government is also silent.
Therefore, in this situation, I want to urge the government, I want to request the government...

I want to tell the Home Minister and the Prime Minister that, whether coming to the rostrum or in the House of Representatives, in both places. We raised this issue yesterday as well. A committee has now been formed regarding the flood in Bhote Koshi. It was discussed in an all-party meeting. For its formation, an all-party committee was formed two or three times. And then that committee was formed. Is the National Assembly a federal parliament or not? If it is a federal parliament, then both the House of Representatives and the National Assembly must have importance, right? The Members of the National Assembly must also have a role, right? If a law needs to be passed, can a law be passed and enacted by the House of Representatives alone? No. The National Assembly also has to pass it, and then it becomes law. Therefore, the House of Representatives and the National Assembly have equal importance. This matter is not a joke to this government. This government is not taking it seriously. We told this to the Chairperson yesterday. The Chairperson had said today that, "I have just spoken with the Chairman of Rastriya Swatantra Party, Rabi Lamichhane. He said that we will form a joint committee in the coming days." Where is it? It wasn't formed today either. What are they trying to do? Are they trying to cheat? Are they trying to deceive? The country cannot be run by deception. The country cannot be run by cheating. You might cheat for a day, you might deceive for a day, but you cannot deceive everyone forever. People might be fooled once, but not forever. Keep this in mind. The current government should keep this in mind. Therefore, I want to speak further with the Chairperson. The way the government is functioning in this country, the way the government has started working in this country. It is neither in favor of good governance, nor in favor of the public. It has not benefited the public, nor has it done good governance. Yes, it is trying to intimidate the public. It is trying to intimidate the traders, the traders are intimidated. Former employees are intimidated, the public is intimidated. Can the country run in this situation? No. In this situation, the country might be scared for a few days if you scare it, but people won't be scared forever. Rana also scared people for 104 years. The king also scared people for 240 years. But they were not scared! Were they scared? They were not scared. Therefore, I want to say that the government should do something in this situation. If it doesn't, then just as we fought for democracy and the people's democracy yesterday, just as we were ready to go to jail for democracy and the people's democracy, we had no personal interest. When we started politics in our student life, we had no self-interest. We had only one self-interest. Sometimes when we went to visit villages, people called us mad. While roaming around like this, they used to call us names. But we didn't worry about that. Why didn't we worry? Because our mission was to bring democracy to the Nepali people. Our mission was not to become honorable individuals. We might become honorable, become ministers, run the country, earn money. People of today might have these thoughts, people who came yesterday might have had them in their minds. But, the situation was not like that when we started politics. When we were doing politics, the communists used to call themselves progressive, and we called ourselves democrats. When we called ourselves democrats, the 'Mandales' used to call us: "Oh, is it Congress?" They immediately caught hold of us if we said Congress. Congress was considered anti-national. It was not a national element, it was an anti-national element. But who is truly the nationalist force in this country? You will understand that now. I clearly remember, when BP Koirala returned in 2033 BS with national reconciliation, someone said yesterday, did BP really try to connect my throat with the King's throat? No, what BP said was, "If the day the republic ends, if the King cuts the throat of democracy, that day the monarchy will not remain. That day the monarchy will collapse. If the King cuts the throat of democracy, the King will collapse." But those who speak now say, "BP was in favor of the King, BP was in favor of the monarchy." That is not true, BP himself spoke and wrote a lot about this. Not only that, when we, the Nepali Congress workers, when BP Koirala went to America for treatment, after being released from jail in 2033 BS. At that time, the King had Bhim Narayan Shrestha killed, and Yadav Bahadur Thapa killed, one in Chakraghatti, one in Kamala. After they were killed, BP then came to Britain. In Britain, the BBC asked him, "You are going back to Nepal, your friends, your friends who were imprisoned with you have been killed by the King. So, if you go, will you face the same treatment?" What did he say? He said, "I have faith in the court, and based on that faith, I will go to Nepal." Today, that faith has also been broken. Yesterday, I had spoken about Dharmendra Bahadur Singh. Dharmendra Bahadur Singh, appointed by the King, when Dr. K.I. Singh faced treason charges, he made this very statement. He ruled that this was not treason. People went to complain to the King about it. The King asked, "The judge appointed by you made such a ruling?" The King did it. Therefore, it is not considered an attempt to seize the throne. We also showed black flags on King Mahendra's birthday. We protested against the King. We also faced treason charges. But after the Supreme Court ruled that if the constitution, the preamble, and their demands are for opening these student organizations, then treason charges do not apply, we were released from Central Jail. Therefore, we were not afraid. Even today, I am not afraid. I want to warn those forces who wish to rule the Nepali people by scaring and intimidating them, that it is not possible. It has already been proven in Nepal's history that those who scare and intimidate have not succeeded. Therefore, I want to say that this government should stop its activities, which are anti-democratic and unpolitical, and should not arrest anyone without a warrant. I remember when I used to be arrested at night, the plainclothes police, when my family members asked if they were police, we didn't believe them. Are you police or some criminals? Otherwise, if they hit and killed us, what would we do at night? So, take us in the morning, in the morning. Today, they are being arrested at night. Sher Bahadur Deuba was also brought in at night from Narayanthan. Therefore, if the current government wants to learn a lesson from the actions of the previous government and wants to operate accordingly, it must stop that, it must abandon that, and it must work within the federal democratic republic constitution that was issued by your Constituent Assembly, and it must act accordingly, I want to say this from this rostrum today. Otherwise, as I said yesterday, if you want to run a party-less system, you have banned all these organizations, you have banned labor unions, you have banned student unions. The labor unions that removed the 104-year-old Rana regime from this country, the students who led the parties when parties were banned outside. You have banned those student organizations. I was reading an article the other day. A university cannot run by banning student organizations. Therefore, what I want to say is that I want to urge and request the current government not to rule by intimidating the Nepali people. You should communicate with the Nepali people. Have conversations. Do not flee from Parliament. Respond to the issues raised in Parliament. Communicate, and only then will democracy and people's democracy be strengthened. Saying this, and considering that the former Chief Justice was also imprisoned, tomorrow they might try to imprison others. But this will not benefit this government. Saying this, I conclude my speech. Thank you. Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai, time 10 minutes. (13:58) After this, Honorable Member Meena Singh Rakhala. Honorable Mr. Jayanti Devi Rai (Communist Party of Nepal):- (13:59) Honorable Chairperson, Sir, before the damage caused to our Bhote Koshi and Rasuwa roads could heal, and before the pain could subside, another pain has been added, and four days of continuous rain have affected all seven provinces across the country. Among them, the Kali Gandaki River in the Mid-West has caused a lot of damage, and in Myagdi, Parbat, Baglung, Mustang, Manang, Palpa, there has been a lot of damage to property and lives, and 21 people have died, and dozens are missing. And in Manang, where a pilgrimage was underway, 14 people are missing and two have died. Therefore, today the entire country is shut down. All roads are closed. No roads to Kathmandu are open. Thousands of energy sources are currently shut down and have been damaged. And today, the Narayani River has actually damaged more than 200 houses in Susta. Similarly, the flow of water in the Kosi region has caused a lot of damage in Sunsari district, and now neither the hills, mountains, the center, the terai, nor the inner terai are safe anywhere in the country. And even the mountains are not safe. Therefore, it is very difficult to live in all these coastal areas, riverine areas. Similarly, in the Indravati River, there are more than 250 households, but they are not willing to move from their birthplace, the place where they have suffered. Therefore, a very dire situation has been created. Therefore, none of us are risk-free today, we are at high risk. Therefore, 28 districts have already been declared, and although there has not been much human loss yet, the government had also been informed in advance, so some attention needs to be paid to such matters, I want to say. We are in a time of disaster, and I am not standing here to criticize the government in this state of disaster, I just want to alert the government that the government needs to coordinate in all aspects, and the problem cannot be solved by running alone, and collective work is strength. Friday, Saturday, Sunday are not coming. There was a time during Janardan's rule when we were afraid to even see the 19th, afraid to see Friday. Now it is the rule of Akon Shah, the two-day holiday has come, and we don't know who will be arrested. What did you consume, what did you take, that makes you do this? I want to ask. Mr. Speaker, before advising others, I urge the Prime Minister and ministers of the government to walk on that path themselves.
There is another issue that I need to raise. On August 31, the Council of Ministers made a decision, and on September 2, the Ministry of Finance issued a circular regarding the daily allowance for the PSOs and drivers of the honorable members and ministers, making it 500 rupees, while the allowance for the Vice President and Deputy Speaker was 75 rupees. It was 75 rupees before, so why does it need to be increased to 500 rupees for the honorable members and ministers? I want to ask. Are they satisfied with 75 rupees? Is this discrimination being done because the Vice President and Deputy Speaker are women? What is this? I want to ask.
Mr. Speaker, I have another issue. During the elections, the friends sang a song, they sang it very well. 'Ghanti tininini, nach phiriri.' In our eastern part, the dance is not 'nach phiriri.' The dance is 'chamchami.' Where did this 'Ghanti tininini, nach phiriri' come from? Now, when I look, after the government came, the situation is that everything has to be 'phiriri.' What is the situation of 'phiriri'? If you buy something from a shop, you get dizzy, you become 'phiriri.' Isn't that what it means? That's what they meant by 'phiriri.' This is not called a dance; it's called dizziness. I thought it was only us who were 'phiriri,' but then the honorable members of the House of Representatives started speaking from the rostrum. They started speaking from the rostrum, saying the canteen is expensive. I want to tell the honorable members, not only your canteen but the people's food and drink have also become expensive. Yesterday, our honorable member asked about this. He asked the minister, showing facts and evidence. The price of sugar is this much, the price of meat is this much, the price of rice is this much. What did the minister reply? We are listening, it's ringing in our ears. Go to such and such a place, and you can get sugar for 110 rupees per kg. Is sugar available for 110 rupees per kg in all parts of the country? This is our question.
Finally, what I want to say is that the Prime Minister said at the United Nations, 'May Pashupatinath protect us all.' I want them to protect us too. If such wisdom had come on the evening of September 9, 2082 (BS), if you had not gone to set Pashupatinath on fire, it would have been a little better. Going to set fire to Pashupatinath, going to attack it, and now asking for Pashupatinath's protection doesn't seem appropriate. I want to urge this point and conclude by thanking you for giving me this time. Namaste, greetings.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar, time 8 minutes.
(14:54 PM)
Honorable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Nepal Communist Party): Honorable Chairperson
(14:54 PM)
It seems like it was searched for. Because of the Bhote Koshi and now in central Nepal, it has caused immense destruction. At least 23 people have died and some are missing. Such a situation has arisen where districts like Manang, Myagdi, Baglung, Palpa, Gulmi, etc., have been severely affected. Now the roads are damaged, festivals are approaching, and this is the situation in the country. The people are distressed and don't know what to do. The government has been in power for 6 months, not just 100 days. This is the time for the government to set its course. If it doesn't take a path now, the government will become like a crow in the fog again.
I will go to a special issue. Who forced Rider Ganesh Nepali, driver Arjun Dodi, and others to self-immolate by setting themselves on fire? Why were they made to have no विकल्प (alternative)? That misfortune happened due to the policies and regulations of this government and the arrogance of this government's soldiers. The elderly Kedar Nath Parajuli of Kavre, unable to treat his wife and finding no alternative, threw his wife into the Sun Koshi river. Such a tragedy has not stopped. Now we are all vigilant, knowing what might happen when. It is not known that the government has expressed concern about stopping these kinds of incidents and solving them in this manner. Life is so difficult, they are living such a difficult life. The government has not been able to give hope and assurance to the people, and the people are now terrified. What to do, how to do it? Big festivals are approaching in Nepal. On one hand, the government talks about good governance, about doing things, and we hear many grand statements, but look now, inflation has reached the sky in the market. The line for gas, the line for going abroad, there are so many such lines. Earlier, they were at least trying to end the lines. This government doesn't even seem to be trying to end the lines. They are just saying that what we have done is done. The unprecedented Himalayan tsunami caused so much damage, and even people who could have been saved were not saved due to the government's incompetence. Even now, bodies are being found when digging in that tunnel, but what does the government say? It says we have done so well, it has gone so well. Even now, we cannot retrieve the expert engineers, the skilled workers inside that tunnel. What does the government think?
In such a situation, it is difficult to manage daily life. The government, the Home Minister, is running abroad seeking help for Nepal, but has achieved nothing. The Prime Minister rushed to the United Nations General Assembly himself. It was expected that he would present a strong issue at the UN General Assembly, but he just shook hands with Secretary-General Guterres on the sidelines and returned. Now, what can we expect? What can we expect from the government? We had thought much more, had many hopes and expectations, but we do not see the government working accordingly. A while ago, the 31st COP conference was held. Now the government has returned from the UN General Assembly. Should the public not be informed through parliament? Should the public not know? And do we have to keep telling this government? Of course, even if we tell them, the government will not listen. The government doesn't even pay attention, but we have provided this information. Now, when ministers, home ministers are asked to come to the parliament, it becomes very difficult. The Home Minister is more likely to be found giving speeches on the street than in parliament, reaching the place where the tunnel collapsed. That is a good thing, but he is neither an engineer nor a skilled worker or laborer, so why does he go there? He might be an administrator, a ruler, a minister. We expect the minister to be in the minister's place, the Prime Minister to be in the Prime Minister's place, and the country to have dignity. Thank you.
Again, Presiding: Honorable Chairperson Shri Narayan Prasad Dahal.
(14:57 PM)
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the special time speaking session ends here.
(15:02 PM)
Honorable members, now I provide time for the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Sovita Gautam, on behalf of the Right Honorable Prime Minister, to present the annual report of the National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission for the fiscal year 2081/082.
Honorable Minister of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Sovita Gautam:-
(15:03 PM)
Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present the annual report of the National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission for the fiscal year 2081/082 to this respected assembly.
Thank you.
